learningGoal.title: Derivative Product Rule
learningGoal.topic: Using the product rule to differentiate products of functions

context.planRationale: This is a conceptual and problem-solving plan for learning the derivative product rule from scratch. It begins with one complete example and one visible step at a time, then moves to guided use, independent retrieval, and mixed application across four 15-minute sessions.

knowledgeTopics.title: Why the Product Rule Works
knowledgeTopics.description: Build a clear model of the product rule and distinguish it from applying the power rule to each factor.
subtopics: Meaning and structure of (fg)' = f'g + fg'

nextSessions.title: Use the Product Rule Step by Step
nextSessions.objective: Carry out the product-rule procedure with guidance, then simplify the result.
contentTargets: Selecting f and g, finding f' and g', substituting, and simplifying

nextSessions.title: Retrieve and Apply the Rule
nextSessions.objective: Use the product rule without a displayed procedure and repair any exposed gap.
contentTargets: Independent recall and application of the product rule

nextSessions.title: Independent Product-Rule Check
nextSessions.objective: Recognize when the product rule is needed and use it independently alongside the familiar power rule.
contentTargets: Choosing between the power rule and product rule

activities.label: Product rule structure
activities.title: Product rule structure
activities.body: Study the rule pattern and its meaning. Then answer the check on the next screen.

essentialIdeas: The derivative of a product is the sum of two parts: first factor times the derivative of the second, plus the derivative of the first times the second.

activities.label: Match each term
activities.title: Match each term
activities.body: Which part means first factor times the derivative of the second?
activities.concept: The derivative of a product is the sum of two parts: first factor times the derivative of the second, plus the derivatve
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the term that keeps the first factor and differentiates the second factor. If needed, restate the full pattern from left to right.

activities.label: Identify the rule
activities.title: Identify the rule
activities.body: Pick the correct derivative rule for a product of two functions.
activities.concept: Meaning and structure of (fg)' = f'g + fg'
activities.feedback: This rule uses two terms, one for each factor taking a turn being differentiated. The other choices confuse product with sum or drop one needed term.

targetAssignments.essentialIdea: The derivative of a product is the sum of two parts: first factor times the derivative of the second, plus the derivative of the first times the second.

items.essentialIdea: The product rule says (fg)' = f'g + fg' for differentiable f and g.

check.title: State the product rule
check.prompt: What is the derivative of a product fg?
check.referenceAnswer: (fg)' = f'g + fg'. The derivative of a product is the sum of f' times g and f times g'.
check.feedback: It splits into two terms, not separate power rule derivatives.

independentCheck.title: Differentiate a product
independentCheck.feedback: Differentiate one factor at a time and add the two results.

recognitionCheck.title: Recognize the product rule
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which formula gives the derivative of a product fg?
recognitionCheck.feedback: The product rule adds two terms, one for each factor being differentiated once.
